Build a transit network graph

Source: R/build_graph.R
build_graph.Rd

Builds a frequency-based transit network from the trips that depart within a time of day, and returns it as a set of tables in the General Modeling Network Specification (GMNS) format or as an {igraph} or {tidygraph} graph. The network can be used in transit assignment models and in graph analyses, such as finding the shortest travel times between stops.

Usage

build_graph(
  gtfs,
  from,
  to,
  format = "gmns",
  max_walk_dist = 300,
  walk_speed = 5
)

Arguments

gtfs

A GTFS object, as created by read_gtfs().

from

A string. The starting point of the time of day, in the "HH:MM:SS" format.

to

A string. The ending point of the time of day, in the "HH:MM:SS" format. Must be later than from.

format

A string. The format of the graph: "gmns" (the default), "igraph" or "tidygraph". The last two require the packages of the same name, which the function offers to install in interactive sessions.

max_walk_dist

A number. The maximum great-circle distance, in meters, between two stops connected by walking transfer links. Defaults to 300.

walk_speed

A number. The walking speed, in km/h, used to calculate the travel time of transfer links. Defaults to 5.

Value

With format = "gmns", a list with the data.tables node, link and config, named after the GMNS files. With format = "igraph", a directed igraph graph, and with format = "tidygraph", a directed tbl_graph. Their vertices and edges have the columns of the node and link tables as attributes, and the name of each vertex is its node_id, as a string.

Details

The network has two types of nodes (node_type):

  • "stop" nodes, one for each stop visited by the trips, placed at the stop's coordinates.

  • "service" nodes, one for each route and direction at each of its stops, placed at the coordinates of the stop (its parent_node_id).

And four types of links (link_type), all of them directed:

  • "in_vehicle" links connect the service nodes of consecutive stops of the trips. Their travel_time is the mean time between the departure from a stop and the arrival at the next one, over the trips with a departure time at the stop and an arrival time at the next one (times that decrease are not used), weighted by the number of departures of each trip, so dwell times are not included. Their departures is the number of departures of the trips of the network (see below) that run through them. Their length is the great-circle distance between the stops, as in get_stop_distances(), and their free_speed is the length divided by the travel time (NA when the travel time is 0 or either is missing).

  • "boarding" links connect each stop to the service nodes from which trips depart. Their departures is the number of departures from the stop of the trips of the network, so it may include departures after to from stops far along their routes. Their travel_time is the mean waiting time: half of the mean headway, which is the length of the time of day divided by the number of departures. Frequency-based assignment models should use departures instead.

  • "alighting" links connect each service node back to its stop, with a travel_time of 0.

  • "transfer" links connect, in both directions, the stops at most max_walk_dist apart. Their travel_time is their length divided by walk_speed, which is also their free_speed.

Lengths are in meters, travel times in minutes and speeds in km/h. Boarding and alighting links have a length of 0 and an NA free_speed, and alighting and transfer links have NA departures. The route_id, direction_id and inferred_direction of in-vehicle, boarding and alighting links are those of their service nodes, and are NA in transfer links.

The network only includes the trips that depart from their first stop at or after from and before to, as in get_route_frequency(), so trips already running at from are not included. The trips listed in the frequencies table are included once for each departure generated from it within the time of day, and their stop_times entries are used as templates. Trips without stop_times entries are not included. The trips of every service_id are pooled together, so the feed should usually be filtered to the services of a single day first, with filter_by_date() or filter_by_weekday(). Departures after midnight are listed with times greater than "24:00:00" and belong to the previous service day, so a time of day such as "24:00:00"-"26:00:00" should be used to account for them. Trips whose times wrongly go back to "00:00:00" after midnight are placed by their earliest time.

Within each trip, consecutive stop_times entries at the same stop are merged into one visit, which arrives at the first known time of the entries and departs at the last one. A trip that visits a stop more than once uses a different service node at each visit (visit 1, 2, ...), so that the network doesn't skip the part of the trip between the visits.

The direction of the trips comes from the direction_id field of trips. The trips without it (or with a blank direction_id) are assigned an inferred_direction instead: the trips of a route that share a pair of consecutive stops, in the same order, are in the same direction, and so are trips that share pairs with them. So branches and short-turns of a route are in the same direction, while the trips that run in opposite directions are not. However, the opposite directions of routes that run through a one-way loop or street, in which they share a pair of stops in the same order, are inferred as a single direction. Trips with a blank direction_id are never assigned the direction of other trips of their route.

In-vehicle links whose trips all have blank or decreasing times have an NA travel_time, which igraph::distances() doesn't accept as a weight. Blank times can be filled beforehand with interpolate_stop_times(). Alighting links, in-vehicle links between stops with the same times and transfer links between stops at the same coordinates have a travel time of 0. igraph::distances() accepts it as a weight, but igraph::closeness() and igraph::betweenness() require positive weights, such as pmax(igraph::E(graph)$travel_time, 1e-6).

Departures are counted at every visit but the last of each trip, even when its departure time is blank, unlike in get_stop_frequency(). The transfers and pathways tables, parent_stations and the pickup_type and drop_off_type fields are not used. Large values of max_walk_dist in dense feeds compare many pairs of stops, which raises a warning when it may use a lot of memory, or an error when there are too many pairs to compare. Transfer links are not created across the antimeridian.

In the GMNS format, node_id, x_coord, y_coord, node_type, parent_node_id, link_id, from_node_id, to_node_id, directed, length and free_speed are GMNS fields. The other columns are fields added by this function, as allowed by GMNS. The config table lists the units and the coordinate reference system (EPSG:4326) of the network, the version of GMNS (0.96) and the time of day. Stops that are not listed in stops, or that don't have coordinates, have NA coordinates. GMNS requires node coordinates, so a warning is raised. Free speeds may be higher than the maximum of 200 km/h checked by GMNS validators, for example in high-speed rail.

See also

The "Building transit network graphs" vignette (vignette("graphs", package = "gtfstools")), which shows how to analyse and plot the network with {igraph}, {tidygraph}, {sfnetworks} and {ggraph}.

Examples

data_path <- system.file("extdata/spo_gtfs.zip", package = "gtfstools")
gtfs <- read_gtfs(data_path)

# the services of every day are pooled together, so only the services of a
# single weekday are kept
gtfs <- filter_by_weekday(gtfs, "wednesday")

graph <- build_graph(gtfs, from = "07:00:00", to = "08:00:00")
names(graph)
#> [1] "node"   "link"   "config"
head(graph$node)
#>    node_id   x_coord   y_coord node_type parent_node_id   stop_id
#>      <int>     <num>     <num>    <char>          <int>    <char>
#> 1:       1 -46.61467 -23.53415      stop             NA 100014307
#> 2:       2 -46.61595 -23.53545      stop             NA 100014308
#> 3:       3 -46.61977 -23.53527      stop             NA 100014309
#> 4:       4 -46.61736 -23.54202      stop             NA 100014321
#> 5:       5 -46.61460 -23.53777      stop             NA 100014331
#> 6:       6 -46.61672 -23.53790      stop             NA 100014332
#>                 stop_name route_id direction_id inferred_direction visit
#>                    <char>   <char>        <int>              <int> <int>
#> 1:    R. Silva Teles, 281     <NA>           NA                 NA    NA
#> 2:     R. Silva Teles, 99     <NA>           NA                 NA    NA
#> 3:  R. João Teodoro, 1331     <NA>           NA                 NA    NA
#> 4: Lgo. Da Concordia, 125     <NA>           NA                 NA    NA
#> 5:        R. Oriente, 760     <NA>           NA                 NA    NA
#> 6:        R. Oriente, 556     <NA>           NA                 NA    NA
head(graph$link)
#>    link_id from_node_id to_node_id directed   length free_speed  link_type
#>      <int>        <int>      <int>   <lgcl>    <num>      <num>     <char>
#> 1:       1          655        656     TRUE 194.1362   6.720098 in_vehicle
#> 2:       2          656        666     TRUE 353.3803  12.232396 in_vehicle
#> 3:       3          657        674     TRUE 447.0238  12.572543 in_vehicle
#> 4:       4          658        672     TRUE 636.0825  22.018241 in_vehicle
#> 5:       5          659        682     TRUE 273.6917  10.481811 in_vehicle
#> 6:       6          660        659     TRUE 216.6252   8.296284 in_vehicle
#>    travel_time departures route_id direction_id inferred_direction
#>          <num>      <int>   <char>        <int>              <int>
#> 1:    1.733333          5  2161-10            0                 NA
#> 2:    1.733333          5  2161-10            0                 NA
#> 3:    2.133333          4  2105-10            1                 NA
#> 4:    1.733333          5  2161-10            0                 NA
#> 5:    1.566667          5  2161-10            1                 NA
#> 6:    1.566667          5  2161-10            1                 NA

# the tables can be written to the csv files of a GMNS network
gmns_dir <- tempfile("gmns")
dir.create(gmns_dir)
for (table in names(graph)) {
  gmns_file <- file.path(gmns_dir, paste0(table, ".csv"))
  data.table::fwrite(graph[[table]], gmns_file)
}
list.files(gmns_dir)
#> [1] "config.csv" "link.csv"   "node.csv"  

# the shortest travel times, in minutes, from a stop to the other stops
graph <- build_graph(
  gtfs,
  from = "07:00:00",
  to = "08:00:00",
  format = "igraph"
)
stop_nodes <- igraph::V(graph)[igraph::V(graph)$node_type == "stop"]
travel_times <- igraph::distances(
  graph,
  v = stop_nodes[1],
  to = stop_nodes,
  mode = "out",
  weights = igraph::E(graph)$travel_time
)

# stops that can't be reached have an infinite travel time
is_reachable <- is.finite(travel_times)
sum(is_reachable)
#> [1] 639
summary(travel_times[is_reachable])
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>    0.00   35.67   53.21   57.91   74.17  167.39
